name: Burkina Faso Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page burk1234 (Burkina Faso Sign Language), with its four reference records (bibtex)
sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference; four refs typed overview or specific_feature. Subclassification note: 'Contra Victoria Nyst (2010):406 and Asonye (2016):787 where it is said to be local, Burkina Faso Sign Language is derived from ASL (Bross 2021, Titus 1994:801)'.

sources.citation: Bross, Fabian. 2021. A brief sketch of the clause structure of Burkina Faso Sign Language (BFSL). Presentation (17 slides) + 2-page abstract, African Sign Languages Workshop, 10th World Congress of African Linguistics, Leiden, 7-12 June 2021. DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/79VCN
sources.note: Nothing on word stress or sign-internal prominence. Syntax only (SVO, interrogatives, negation, modals, temporal adverbs); the only prosodic remark is slide 9: 'Polar interrogatives are formed by raised eye-brows... Intensity peak of the NMMs is clause-final.' Signs 'mainly borrowed from ASL', mouthings from French; author calls BFSL 'an ASL creole, which is currently emerging'.

sources.citation: Sanogo, Yédê Adama & Nobutaka Kamei. 2019. La promotion de la recherche sur la Langue des Signes par les communautés des Sourds africains: cas de l'Afrique de l'Ouest et de Centre francophone. Journal of Cultural Symbiosis Research 13: 5-16. DOI 10.15088/00003764
sources.note: Nothing. History/sociolinguistics of Langue des Signes d'Afrique Francophone (LSAF, ASL-based creole); Burkina Faso mentioned only as an LSAF country (Ouagadougou CMD school) and via the manual SWB-CI (ed.) 2014a 'Manuel de langue des signes, EFTP-Burkina Faso', Lomé: CBM.

sources.citation: サノゴ・イェデ・アダマ & 亀井伸孝 (Sanogo & Kamei). 2015. アフリカろう者コミュニティによる手話言語研究の促進. 手話学研究 (Japanese Journal of Sign Language Studies) 24: 3-16. DOI 10.7877/jasl.24.3
sources.note: Nothing; Japanese version of the same report; Burkina Faso named only as a fieldwork country and manual target.

sources.note: Stubs; cite only Nyst 2010:406 and Bross 2021; 'considered to be an ASL based creole language'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kamei, Nobutaka. 2006. The birth of Langue des Signes Franco-Africaine: Creole ASL in West and Central French-speaking Africa. Online conference paper, Languages and Education in Africa Conference (LEA2006), University of Oslo.
sources.note: UiO conference URL now returns the department home page; CiNii record only. Argues LSAF is an ASL-based creole across francophone Africa incl. Burkina Faso; not BFSL-specific.
